newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SHANAHAN OT GOAL GIVES BOWMAN 1,000TH COACHING WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SHANAHAN OT GOAL GIVES BOWMAN 1,000TH COACHING WIN.

text.p: Brendan Shanahan completed his ninth career hat trick 2:01 into overtime Saturday to give the Detroit Red Wings a 6-5 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins and Scotty Bowman his 1,000th regular season coaching victory.

After two failed attempts to hand Bowman his unprecedented milestone victory, Shanahan ended the shootout with his third goal of the game and 32nd of the season, beating Patrick Lalime with a wrist shot on Detroit's 47th shot on goal.
That the historic victory came against one of Bowman's former clubs was not lost on the Red Wings.

"They're gonna be talking about this win for years," Shanahan said. "I think to win here in Pittsburgh, where (Bowman) was a coach, was exciting for all of us. I just wanted to make sure I didn't miss the net."
Bowman coached the Penguins to a Stanley Cup in 1992, the fifth NHL championship of a 25-year coaching career with St Louis, Montreal, Buffalo Pittsburgh and Detroit.

The Penguins led four times, twice taking the lead on goals by Mario Lemieux -- his 38th and 39th. But Detroit came back each time with Daren McCarty tying the game, 5-5, at 13:49 of the third with an assist by Shanahan.

Lemieux nearly won the game in overtime, as he deked out the Detroit defence while driving to the net with the puck. But his nifty pass also surprised teammate Ron Francis in the slot and the puck slid past the Detroit net.
"It didn't look too good," Shanahan said of Lemieux's overtime rush. "We all kind of held our breath."
On Long Island, Mark Messier recorded his 19th career hat trick to lead the New York Rangers to a 5-2 win over their local rivals, the New York Islanders.
Alexander Karpovtsev and former Islanders captain Patrick Flatley had the other goals for the Rangers as goaltender Mike Richter improved to 19-3-2 in his last 24 decisions.
Wayne Gretzky failed to get a goal for the 16th straight game, matching the longest drought of his career. But his assist on Karpovtsev's goal gave the Great One 19 assists in his last 15 games.
At Colorado, Alexei Zhamnov and Eric Daze put slap shots past All-Star goaltender Patrick Roy and Jeff Hackett made 30 saves as the Chicago Blackhawks beat the Avalanche 4-2.

Zhamnov scored with 6:37 to go in the second period to snap a 1-1 tie. Daze scored on a powerplay just under seven minutes into the third for a two goal cushion as the Blackhawks won for the fourth time in five games.
In Boston, Jean-Yves Roy beat Grant Fuhr with 72 seconds left in regulation as the Bruins rallied from a three-goal deficit to forge a 3-3 tie with the St Louis Blues.
Tim Sweeney and Rick Tocchet also scored for Boston after Harry York, Ricard Persson and Pierre Turgeon gave the Blues a 3-0 lead that held up until the middle of the second period.

At New Jersey, Valeri Zelepukin and Bobby Holik scored less than two minutes apart early in a three-goal third period to give the Devils a 4-2 win over the Philadelphia Flyers, who lost for the first time when leading after two periods.

Steve Sullivan scored the Devils other third-period goal, while Eric Lindros and Daniel Lacroix scored in the second period for Philadelphia, which had been 19-0-1 when carrying a lead into the third period this season.
In Montreal, Stephane Richer got the tying goal with 2:37 left in regulation and Brian Savage scored 61 seconds into overtime to lift the Canadiens to a 3-2 victory over the Hartford Whalers.
Paul Ranheim and Geoff Sanderson had given Hartfor a 2-1 lead with third-period goals. Mark Recchi scored the first Montreal goal in the second period.
Jose Theodore stopped 22 shots for Montreal, while Sean Burke made 33 saves for Hartford.
In Ottawa, Steve Guolla scored two third-period goals in a 4:23 span as the San Jose Sharks rallied for a 3-3 tie with the Ottawa Senators.
Alexei Yashin had a goal and an assist for Ottawa, which led 3-1 after two periods and set a franchise record by stretching its unbeaten streak to four games.
Kelly Hrudey faced only 15 shots, including four in the third period and overtime, for San Jose.
At Tampa Bay, Matthew Barnaby scored twice and Dominik Hasek made 31 saves to lead the Buffalo Sabres to a 3-1 win over the Lightning.
Hasek stoppped all 26 shots he faced over the first two periods as Buffalo improved to 3-0-3 in its last six games to move within one point of first-place Pittsburgh in the Northeast Division.
Roman Hamrlik broke up Hasek's shutout bid with a powerplay goal at 9:28 of the third period.
In Toronto, Kirk Muller and Mats Sundin each had a goal and an assist and Felix Potvin turned aside 28 shots as the Maple Leafs beat the Vancouver Canucks 4-2.
Tie Domi and Nathan Dempsey also scored for the Leafs. Dempsey's goal was his first NHL point and gave Toronto a 4-0 lead late in the second period.
Jyrki Lumme and Mike Ridley scored in the third for the Canucks, who have lost four of their last five games.
In Phoenix, Pat Verbeek tied the game late in the third period and scored 3:50 into overtime to lift the Dallas Stars to a 5-4 victory over the stunned Coyotes.

Phoenix scored four times in the second period to take a 4-0 lead, but Dallas stormed back with five unanswered goals, including three in the third, as they peppered Coyotes goalie Nikolai Khabibulin with 50 shots on goal.
In Edmonton, Teemu Selanne scored his 31st goal 45 seconds into overtime to give the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim a 2-1 victory over the Oilers.
Bobby Dollas scored 8:42 into the third period to tie the game for Anaheim. Andrei Kovalenko scored the lone goal for Edmonton, a power-play tally at 12:25 of the first period.
